title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False
tldr: A deterministic algorithm counts the satisfying assignments of any $k$-CNF in subexponential time and polynomial space; the case $k = 3$ refutes ETH.

millennium.note: Refutes ETH, SETH, #ETH, Gap-ETH and NSETH. A subexponential running time can still be superpolynomial, so P vs NP stays open.

status.note: OpenAI reports a Lean 4 proof of the top-line theorem (with the weaker exponent $n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n}$), checked against a published statement file. An independent working group led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams is examining the proof.

title: Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank
short_title: Exact BSD formula in low rank
tldr: Claims the complete Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula, with every prime factor exact, for every elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ whose Selmer group at some prime has corank $0$ or $1$, with no further hypotheses on the curve.

millennium.note: Settles the conjecture, including the exact leading-term formula and finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group, for curves of rank $0$ or $1$ in the Selmer sense. Curves of rank $2$ or more are untouched.

status.note: First posted 3 October 2026 and released with OpenAI's batch of manuscripts on 6 October; the 7 October edition only drops a citation and updates references. The proof depends on three companion OpenAI manuscripts (a low-corank converse, the two-primary formula and Goldfeld's twist densities, about 380 pages together), which are also unreviewed. There is no Lean formalization. We found no public expert assessment as of this date.

title: The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
short_title: Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
tldr: Claims the Hodge conjecture for every complex abelian variety with complex multiplication, in every dimension and codimension, and through theorems of Milne the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields.

millennium.note: Proves the conjecture for one important family of shapes, CM abelian varieties and their products, where exotic Hodge classes not built from divisors do occur. The conjecture for general varieties stays open.

status.note: First posted 30 September 2026 and released with OpenAI's batch of manuscripts on 6 October; the 6 October edition only updates a citation. OpenAI added a Lean 4 formalization of the main theorem on 26 October (we have not re-run it); the consequences for the Tate and standard conjectures are outside its scope. On 6 and 7 October OpenAI withdrew three other Hodge-related manuscripts after a sign error; this paper does not cite them. We found no public expert assessment as of this date.

title: The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: a zero-free half-plane Re(s) > 7/8
tldr: Claims that the Riemann zeta function and every Dirichlet $L$-function have no zeros with real part above $7/8$, a fixed margin from the edge that holds at every height and for every character, which mathematicians call the quasi-Riemann hypothesis.

millennium.note: Keeps every zero of zeta between real parts $1/8$ and $7/8$; the Riemann hypothesis asks for exactly $1/2$ and stays open. If right, it also removes Landau–Siegel zeros and settles Vinogradov's conjecture on the least quadratic nonresidue.

status.note: Dated 30 September 2026 and released with OpenAI's batch of manuscripts on 6 October. OpenAI published a Lean 4 formalization of the 7/8 statement for zeta, for all Dirichlet $L$-functions and for the Hecke family; we have not re-run it. A shorter companion proving 11/12, written with human assistance, followed on 5 October. Quanta (19 October) reports that number theorists are working through the proof and that Peter Sarnak is teaching a course on it. Banks, Kerr and Green have posted independent reworkings of the related Landau–Siegel argument. No error has been reported as of this date, and no journal has reviewed it.

title: The Unique Games Theorem
tldr: Claims a proof of Khot's Unique Games Conjecture, which would make the best known approximation algorithms for Max-Cut, Vertex Cover and many other problems provably optimal unless P = NP.

millennium.note: Does not decide whether P equals NP. It shows that many approximation problems are exactly as hard as NP problems, so their best known algorithms cannot be improved unless P = NP.

status.note: Dated 23 September 2026 and released with OpenAI's batch of manuscripts on 6 October. OpenAI published Lean 4 formalizations of the main reduction and of the direct Max-Cut, Vertex Cover, Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set hardness results (we have not re-run them). Press and blog coverage in October reports that experts including Dana Moshkovitz, Subhash Khot, Johan Håstad and Dor Minzer were studying the proof, without a settled verdict; we could not open those sources directly. No error has been reported to our knowledge.

title: Finite Time Blowup for Navier–Stokes
tldr: For every viscosity, a smooth force that is switched on for a while drives a fluid starting at rest to unbounded speed at time 1 with bounded energy, which would settle the Clay problem through its breakdown alternatives (C) and (D).

millennium.note: Claims breakdown alternatives (C) and (D) of the official problem, which allow a smooth, decaying force. Whether flows with no force can break down stays open. The Clay Institute has not ruled.

status.note: OpenAI published a Lean 4 formalization (about 429,000 lines) of both breakdown statements, checked against an adaptation of the Formal Conjectures statement of the problem; we have not re-run it. Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen (arXiv 2610.08144, 6 October 2026) show that parts of the Lean proof follow different arguments, and sometimes prove different intermediate bounds, from the written paper; they make no claim that the written proof is wrong. The Clay Institute says it is evaluating the claim. This explainer was checked against the paper's Sections 1-3 (introduction, physical description, proof outline).

title: Perelman's Ricci flow papers: the proof of the Poincaré conjecture
tldr: Three arXiv preprints (2002–03) that finish Richard Hamilton's program: let a shape smooth itself by its own curvature (Ricci flow), cut out the thin necks that form, and show that a closed three-dimensional shape in which every loop can be shrunk dies out in finite time, which forces it to be the three-sphere.

millennium.note: Proves the conjecture (and, with more work, Thurston's geometrization conjecture). The Clay Institute awarded the prize in 2010; Perelman declined it. The smooth four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture is a different question and is still open.

status.note: Perelman posted three preprints to arXiv (November 2002, March 2003, July 2003) and never submitted them to a journal. Three teams wrote out the missing details in 2006: Kleiner and Lott (notes, published 2008), Morgan and Tian (a book, 2007) and Cao and Zhu (2006). Colding and Minicozzi gave an independent proof of the finite extinction step. Perelman declined the Fields Medal in 2006, and the Clay Institute awarded him the Millennium Prize on 18 March 2010, which he also declined. We know of no complete computer-checked proof.
